pr_body:
Fixes #19511

This is one potential approach for allowing GLTFLoader to utilize ImageBitmaps, which significantly reduce stalls in rendering when uploading textures to the GPU. Alternatively, if allowing a custom ImageLoader to be supplied to the TextureLoader is not desirable, we could use ImageBitmapLoader and CanvasTexture in this class directly when ImageBitmaps are supported and fallback to TextureLoader otherwise.

The reason this is limited to GLTFLoader for now is that ImageBitmap-based textures don't support Y-flipping in the same way that the traditional approach does. If a workaround is figured out for that then ImageBitmaps could be used more widely.
pr_comments:
It's worth noting that ImageBitmapLoader depends on `fetch()` rather than `XmlHttpRequest`. I think that's OK in terms of browser support — browsers like IE11 that don't support `fetch` won't support `createImageBitmap` either, and so won't try to use this feature. But our use of `fetch()` does not include any HTTP request headers...

https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/400acd3c78c8e631087322eb1e0e9fc00a16b375/src/loaders/ImageBitmapLoader.js#L69

...which could be a problem for some users who specify them. We should probably try to pass those request parameters into the `fetch()` call.

Starting with `GLTFLoader` seemed like a good idea until I saw we have to add new API (`setImageLoader`)...

> The reason this is limited to GLTFLoader for now is that ImageBitmap-based textures don't support Y-flipping in the same way that the traditional approach does. If a workaround is figured out for that then ImageBitmaps could be used more widely.

I think it may be better to try to implement glsl based Y-flipping and then implement this right in `TextureLoader`. Probably after taking care of #17949 though.

An alternate route to adding this would be to have the glTF loader internally use TextureLoader on browsers that don't support ImageBitmaps and ImageBitmapLoader + CanvasTextures on browsers that do. That felt messier to me, but if we're trying to keep new API surface off of TextureLoader at all costs it's a more self contained approach.
I'd be OK with @toji's suggestion of just putting it on GLTFLoader for now, without a new API. Might be a safer place to start, and see if there are any browser support edge cases we've missed?
Okay, updated the PR to a variant that doesn't alter `TextureLoader` at all. Let me know how it looks!

@toji FYI, this PR broke model-viewer. I've fixed it by passing `{ premultiplyAlpha: 'none' }` to `createImageBitmap` by default: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/commit/7e5d14894e6ef57007faf5903d713b85c97801ef

@jdashg FYI, I had to add Firefox UA sniffing because the current implementation of `createImageBitmap` breaks when passing `{ premultiplyAlpha: 'none' }` as options: 70aed3c8092392b73083e1d403ab9a90e4caa975
Should have a user-facing option to disable the ImageBitmapLoader? I wonder if there may be other browser compatibility issues...
I've tested Safari too. Seems like it's not shipping `createImageBitmap` yet.

Ooof, sorry about that! I know @fernandojsg and @daoshengmu and @takahirox were looking into this, e.g., for:
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1367251
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1367251

Blech. Sorry for missing the premultiplied alpha bit, but I'm glad the fix was trivial. And yes, Safari hasn't shipped `createImageBitmap` yet, which is 😢 but at least lends itself to clean feature detection.

issue_context.title: Use ImageBitmaps for GLTFLoader (and possibly others)
comments: BTW: I'm happy to put up a pull request to make this change, but I wanted to ensure it was something that the maintainers approved of first and that any potential pitfalls or alternate approaches could be discussed.

We investigated this a few years ago (https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/12456). At the time, support was good in Chrome, but (a) significantly limited in Firefox, and (b) quite broken in Safari. I am able to see https://threejs.org/examples/?q=imagebitmap#webgl_loader_imagebitmap in both Safari and Firefox now, so perhaps this has improved. Do you know which browsers your GLTFLoader change would support?

> So it's safe to use ImageBitmapLoader in that context while continuing to use ImageLoader everywhere else. I imagine this would be the case for many model formats...

Searching `examples/js/loaders` for occurrences of `flipY`, it appears to be only GLTFLoader and MMDLoader that can guarantee `flipY=false`.

> Do you know which browsers your GLTFLoader change would support?

It's working for me in Chromium based browsers and Firefox. I thought it was working on iOS as well, but having just checked it again I'm now seeing some failures. (May have been lulled into a false sense of security by the browser cache. Wouldn't be the first time.) I'll try to do some additional debugging on that. Regardless, this may still be worth investigating on a whitelist basis since the improvement can be so dramatic.

> Searching examples/js/loaders for occurrences of flipY, it appears to be only GLTFLoader and MMDLoader that can guarantee flipY=false

That's mildly surprising. But also, doesn't MMD primarily use TGAs? If so I imagine that `ImageBitmap`s wouldn't apply because you'd be creating `DataTexture`s out of the JS-decoded image.

> Turns out this only works for glTF files or similar formats where the texture usage is well defined. In other cases where the textures are being applied to dynamically generated meshes they have an annoying tendency to come in upside down because ImageBitmap texture sources ignore the gl.UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL parameter, and the flipY option that they do support must be set at load time, while THREE.Texture allows it to be set at any time.

Maybe it's time to move away from `gl.UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL` and do the flipping in glsl: `1.0 - uv.y`.

Sounds good to me that we use ImageBitmapLoader in case where it works fine without any problems. In addition to the performance improvement, it also has advantage that it works in Workers. (ImageLoader doesn't work in the Workers.)

Okay, so my Safari issue was due to a [really dumb mistake](https://github.com/toji/xr-dinosaurs/commit/f7a737092c8f1201dbc0c3f49efb7337880e11e6) on my part. 😓 

Good news is, though, that after fixing that my code appears to be working on every browser I've tested.

> Okay, so my Safari issue was due to a [really dumb mistake](https://github.com/toji/xr-dinosaurs/commit/f7a737092c8f1201dbc0c3f49efb7337880e11e6) on my part. 😓 

Haha, I saw the code and I thought... `unknown`? Yet another JS thing I've never heard of 😁

> Maybe it's time to move away from gl.UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL and do the flipping in glsl: 1.0 - uv.y.

Sounds a good idea. It would resolve this issue, too #16144
